subject: Redwood quickstart & env plan — next steps for SDK onramp
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood quickstart & env plan — next steps for SDK onramp

Hi Alex / Samir —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed plan to get Lumina onto a local SDK pilot (Python + TS) so your infra team can validate auth, routing, and our structured-output/tool-calling paths before any Dedicated sizing. High level:

- Goal: run the Redwood SDK sample apps locally, exercise auth (API keys + short-lived tokens), test request routing and structured output (tool calls) and validate embeddings/reranking on a small dataset.
- Timebox: 2-week sandbox sprint (benchmarks + smoke tests) with a follow-up demo at the end.

Immediate asks from Lumina (per the call):
1) Confirm which environment you want to run first — dev laptop (Docker) or a small EC2 test instance.
2) Provide the list of IP ranges for egress allowlist if you plan to call our hosted endpoints.
3) Point us to a small sample of documents (100–500 rows) for embeddings + rerank sanity checks (anonymized).

What Redwood will deliver by end of week:
- A tailored quickstart checklist (attached) and a small ZIP with two sampleapps (python-flask + ts-express) that exercise: auth, streaming, structured tool-calls, and an embeddings->rerank pipeline.
- A short network diagram showing expected ports and recommended proxy config (attached).
- A runbook for local testing with test prompts and expected verification checks (latency & correctness).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm env choice (laptop vs EC2) and provide egress ranges by Thu 7/27.
- Redwood schedules a 60-min hands-on session (we pair-program the quickstart) for next Tue or Wed.

I'll drop the quickstart artifacts and the GitHub sample repo link in a follow up in case you want to preview before the session.

Thanks,
Soojin
--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0169
Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin — good summary. A couple quick answers:

- We'll start on an EC2 t3.medium test instance in our dev VPC (easier to share with infra).
- Egress: our NAT gateway covers 3.82.16.0/22 and 35.128.0.0/10; I'll confirm with infra if they need the full set of ranges or if this is sufficient.
- We'll scrub and share a 250-row anonymized sample next business day.

A couple of follow-ups from our side:
- Can the quickstart run fully offline (i.e., connecting to a private Redwood Dedicated instance) or does it require calls to hosted endpoints for license/auth checks? We prefer to validate local behavior first.
- Curious what the structured output tooling looks like for tool calling — is it just JSON schemas or do you provide a helper that wires into external services (HTTP/webhook) for tool execution?

We like the Tuesday slot for the hands-on. Any time between 10–13 PDT works.

— Alex
Alex Duarte
Lead Integrations Engineer, Lumina Health
alex.duarte@luminahealth.com

Alex —

Short answers:
- Quickstart offline: the sampleapps include a local-mode that talks to a customer-provisioned Redwood Private endpoint (we supply a small dev token flow). No mandatory calls to hosted license endpoints; there is an optional health-check you can call to pull performance profiles. We'll include instructions in the runbook.
- Structured output/tool-calling: two layers — (1) a schema-first runner that validates model output against a JSON schema (we provide helpers in both Python/TS), and (2) an optional execution adapter that will make HTTP calls or enqueue messages to your webhook/topic if model output includes an action. The sampleapps demonstrate both behaviors with a mock webhook.

I've uploaded the checklist, network diagram, and a ZIP of the sampleapps to the Drive link below. The repo contains:
- python-flask/sample_app.py -> auth via short-lived token, example of structured-tool call flow, embeddings client
- ts-express/src/server.ts -> streaming + tool-caller middleware, reranker example using embeddings vector store
- tests/local_smoke.md -> a short checklist of 12 smoke checks you can run locally (auth, streaming, structured output validation, embeddings sanity, rerank relevance)

Drive / repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapps/tree/quickstart/lumina

Can we lock Tuesday 7/31 at 10:30 PDT for the paired session? Ben will run the demo and Karthik will own the embeddings/rerank tech checks.

Action items assigned:
- Alex/Samir: confirm EC2 instance ready + egress confirmation (by 7/28).
- Redwood (Ben): prepare a short test dataset and a runbook tailored to Lumina (by 7/28).
- Karthik: package a small rerank baseline and expected metrics sheet (by 7/30).

If that all looks good I will send a calendar invite and a Zoom link.

Thanks,
Soojin

Subject: Re: Redwood quickstart & env plan — next steps for SDK onramp

Quick confirmation from my side — prepping the sample dataset and the local-smoke test matrix now. A couple technical notes for Alex's infra team ahead of the session:

- Ports: the sampleapps use 3000 (TS) and 5000 (Python) by default. If you run behind a proxy, make sure streaming responses are not buffered (we recommend chunked transfer).
- Token flow: we'll give you a tiny script that mints a dev token (expires in 1 hour) so you can validate auth rotation without touching your PKI.
- Embeddings store: the rerank demo uses a lightweight in-memory vector store. For a longer trial we can show a Redis + vector extension pattern.

I'll attach the smoke-run checklist to the calendar invite. Looking forward to pairing.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
